entities.summary: Diogo Afonso was a Portuguese explorer and political leader of the 15th century, renowned for his pivotal role in the Age of Exploration. Born into a noble family in Portugal around 1450, Afonso was educated in the arts of navigation and warfare, and by 1482, he had become a trusted advisor to King John II of Portugal. As the king's emissary, Afonso led several expeditions to explore the African coast, establishing trade routes and mapping the coastline of West Africa. His journeys not only expanded Portugal's influence but also laid the groundwork for the country's future maritime dominance. Afonso's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his expeditions paved the way for subsequent Portuguese explorers, including Vasco da Gama, who famously circumnavigated the globe in 1497. The impact of Afonso's voyages can still be felt today, with the legacy of Portuguese colonialism still present in many African countries. Afonso's life is a testament to the power of determination and vision, inspiring future generations of explorers and leaders.
